title: Colimit of localizations
statement:
Let $K$ be a commutative ring and let $B$ be an integral $K$-algebra (a commutative $K$-algebra with $1\ne0$ and no zero divisors) which is a filtered union $B=\bigcup_{i\in I}B_i$ of its finite type $K$-subalgebras [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Here $I$ is a set, the family is nonempty, and any two $B_i,B_j$ are contained in some $B_k$. Put $L=\mathrm{Frac}(B)$, the field of fractions: its elements are $a/b$ with $a,b\in B$, $b\ne0$, where $a/b=c/d$ means $ad=bc$, with the usual addition and multiplication of fractions. In particular $B$ embeds in $L$ by $a\mapsto a/1$; no algebraic closedness is required.
Let $J$ be the set of pairs $(i,g)$ with $i\in I$ and $g\in B_i\setminus\{0\}$, preordered by $(i',g')\ge(i,g)$ if and only if $B_i\subseteq B_{i'}$ and the image of $g$ in $(B_{i'})_{g'}$ is a unit, where $(B_i)_g=B_i[1/g]$ is the principal localization [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Regard this preorder as a small category with a unique arrow when the relation holds. With the canonical $K$-algebra transition maps extending the subalgebra inclusions, it is filtered, and the canonical embeddings into $L$ exhibit
$$L\cong\varinjlim_{(i,g)\in J}(B_i)_g$$
as a colimit in commutative rings (and in commutative $K$-algebras), in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

proof.text: For $p=(i,g)$ define $e_p:(B_i)_g\to L$ by $a/g^n\mapsto a/g^n$. The fraction relation in [def-weil-ring-localization-away] implies $g^k(ag^m-bg^n)=0$ in $B_i$ for equal representatives; since $g\ne0$ in the domain $B$, cancel $g^k$ to get the fraction equality in $L$. The displayed addition and multiplication formulas make $e_p$ a ring map; it sends the image $c/1$ of each $c\in K$ to the same scalar in $L$, so it is a $K$-algebra map. It is injective: equality in $L$ says $ag^m=bg^n$ in $B$, hence in its subring $B_i$, so the localization relation holds with exponent $k=0$. Thus identify $(B_i)_g$ with its image $A_p\subseteq L$.

source.place: Proof, sentence "Every $(B_i)_g$ injects into $L$", expanded by the fraction relation (Stacks Tag 00CO).

proof.text: If $p=(i,g)\le q=(j,h)$, let $u$ be the inverse of $g$ in $(B_j)_h$ and define $t_{pq}(a/g^n)=a u^n$. If $g^k(ag^m-bg^n)=0$ represents equality in the source, its image in the target gives $a g^m=b g^n$ after multiplying by $u^k$; multiplying further by $u^{m+n}$ proves independence of the representative. For addition the fraction formula [def-weil-ring-localization-away] gives $(ag^m+bg^n)u^{n+m}=au^n+bu^m$, and for multiplication it gives $(ab)u^{n+m}=(au^n)(bu^m)$; the map fixes $0,1$ and all scalars. Thus $t_{pq}$ is a $K$-algebra map. Any ring map extending $B_i\subseteq B_j$ must send $1/g$ to $u$, since it must send $g(1/g)=1$ to $gu=1$; its values on $a/g^n$ are therefore forced, so this extension is unique. Its composite with $e_q$ is $e_p$, since the image of $u$ in $L$ is $g^{-1}$. Thus $A_p\subseteq A_q$ and $t_{pq}$ is that inclusion under the embeddings; identities and compositions are consequently identities and compositions of inclusions.

source.place: Proof, implicit diagram of localizations: explicit transition maps and their compatibility; Stacks Tag 00CO fraction formulas.

proof.text: The relation is reflexive since $g$ is invertible in $(B_i)_g$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. It is transitive: if $p\le q\le r$, the map $t_{qr}$ sends the inverse of $g$ in the $q$-stage to an inverse in the $r$-stage, and subalgebra inclusions compose. There is a pair $(i,1)$ because the family is nonempty and $1\ne0$. For $(i,g),(j,h)$ choose $k$ containing both subalgebras. The product $gh\in B_k$ is nonzero since $B$ is a domain. In $(B_k)_{gh}$ the fractions $h/(gh)$ and $g/(gh)$ invert $g$ and $h$, respectively. Hence $(k,gh)$ is a common upper bound. Parallel arrows in the thin category are equal and the identity on their target equalizes them, so these facts verify all filteredness conditions of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]; $J$ is small because it is a set of pairs.

source.place: Proof, first sentence "The order is filtered", including the nonempty and parallel-arrow clauses of Stacks Tag 002V.

proof.text: Every $x\in L$ has the form $a/b$ with $a\in B$ and $0\ne b\in B$ by the stated construction of the fraction field. The union hypothesis puts $a$ and $b$ in two stages, and directedness puts both in one $B_i$. The element $a/b\in(B_i)_b$ of [def-weil-ring-localization-away] maps to $x$. This also covers $x=0$ by taking $a=0,b=1$. Therefore the subrings $A_p$ cover $L$.

source.place: Proof, last sentence "Conversely, for $a/b\in L$ ...", corrected to allow the numerator to be zero.

proof.text: Let $R$ be any commutative ring and let $(v_p:(B_i)_g\to R)_p$ be a compatible cocone. For $x\in A_p$ set $v(x)=v_p(e_p^{-1}(x))$. If also $x\in A_q$, choose a common upper bound $r$ from step 3. The two representatives have the same image in the $r$-stage by injectivity of $e_r$, so cocone compatibility gives the same value in $R$. This defines $v$ on all of $L$ by step 4. For $x,y$ choose a stage containing both; its map $v_r$ preserves their sum and product and $0,1$, so $v$ is a ring map. Every factorization must have these values on each $A_p$, hence is unique. If $R$ is a commutative $K$-algebra and every $v_p$ is a $K$-algebra map, the same formula preserves every scalar, so it also proves the $K$-algebra assertion. Together with $e_qt_{pq}=e_p$, this is exactly the colimit universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

source.place: Proof, middle sentence "so the colimit is a subring of $L$" and final equality, replaced by the explicit universal property (Stacks Tag 002F).
